paragraphs.title: A Plea for Protection from the Enemy

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer.”
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist speak?

easy.explanation: He asks God to “preserve my life from fear of the enemy.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to preserve?

easy.explanation: He says, “Hear my voice, O God, in my prayer.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to hear?

answers: Because he wants to leave the city
medium.explanation: The verse specifically mentions “fear of the enemy.”
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask God to preserve his life?

medium.explanation: The psalmist asks God to protect his life from the enemy’s fear.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does the word “preserve” mean in this passage?

answers: He asks God to hear him and then to preserve his life
He asks God to punish the enemy and then to give him riches
He asks God to hide the enemy and then to make him king
medium.explanation: First he says, “Hear my voice,” and then asks God to preserve his life.
medium.q: What is the order of the psalmist’s requests?

answers: Fear joined with prayer for God’s help
Complete confidence that no danger exists
challenge.explanation: The psalmist mentions fear of the enemy while turning to God in prayer.
challenge.q: What central feeling is expressed in these verses?

answers: The prayer concerns a real danger to the psalmist’s life
The psalmist stops speaking about himself
The prayer is only about the enemy’s life
challenge.explanation: He asks God both to hear his voice and to protect his life.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “my voice” to “my life” suggest?

answers: That God would preserve his life
That God would explicitly punish the enemy
challenge.explanation: The verses ask for hearing and protection, but do not explicitly request punishment.
challenge.q: Which request does not appear in these verses?

paragraphs.title: Hidden Plots and Weapons of Speech

easy.explanation: The passage speaks of shooting “in secret” and laying snares “privily.”
easy.q: Where do the wicked make their plans?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “Who whet their tongue like a sword.”
easy.q: What is the tongue of the wicked compared to?

easy.explanation: They plan “to shoot in secret at the perfect.”
easy.q: At whom do the wicked secretly shoot?

answers: They use sharp and bitter words
medium.explanation: Their tongues are compared to swords, and their arrows represent “bitter words.”
medium.q: How do the wicked use speech to harm others?

answers: They make their words sharp and hurtful
They speak only words of praise
medium.explanation: The image of sharpening a sword describes speech prepared to wound.
medium.q: What does the expression “whet their tongue like a sword” mean?

answers: They conspire, speak bitterly, and lay hidden snares
They confess, repent, and ask forgiveness
They flee, surrender, and stop making plans
medium.explanation: The passage describes secret counsel, harmful speech, and snares laid privily.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the actions of the wicked?

answers: They think their hidden deeds will not be discovered
They want everyone to praise them
They are afraid to speak to one another
challenge.explanation: Their question shows confidence that no one will see their secret plans.
challenge.q: What does the question “Who shall see them?” reveal about the wicked?

answers: Their harmful speech is pictured as arrows that wound
The arrows are used only for protection
challenge.explanation: The passage presents arrows and “bitter words” as instruments of secret attack.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between their arrows and their bitter words?

answers: Their inward thoughts and intentions are hidden and difficult to know
They are filled with joyful thoughts
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes the depth and secrecy of their inward thoughts and hearts.
challenge.q: What does “the heart is deep” suggest about the wicked?

paragraphs.title: The Plot Turns Against Its Makers

answers: He shoots at them with an arrow
easy.explanation: The KJV says, “But God shall shoot at them with an arrow.”
easy.q: What does God do to the wicked?

answers: It causes them to fall upon themselves
easy.explanation: Their own tongue is made “to fall upon themselves.”
easy.q: What happens to the tongue of the wicked?

answers: They fear and declare His work
easy.explanation: The passage says, “all men shall fear, and shall declare the work of God.”
easy.q: How do people respond to God’s work?

answers: The weapons and words of the wicked turn against them
Fear changes into joy without any cause
medium.explanation: God’s arrow wounds them, and their own tongue falls upon them.
medium.q: What is the main reversal in these verses?

medium.explanation: Those who see what happens flee away, showing their alarm and fear.
medium.q: In this context, what does “flee away” mean?

answers: They witness the downfall of the wicked
medium.explanation: After seeing the judgment, people fear and declare God’s work.
medium.q: What leads people to recognize God’s work?

answers: Their hidden scheme does not remain hidden and finally works against them
Their plot is shown never to have existed
challenge.explanation: The attack they planned is reversed, and their own words bring them down.
challenge.q: How is the downfall of the wicked connected to their original plot?

answers: The judgment comes unexpectedly, just as the wicked planned to attack suddenly
The wicked announce their defeat beforehand
The arrow has no connection to the plot
challenge.explanation: The wicked planned a sudden attack, but God’s sudden arrow strikes them instead.
challenge.q: What does the sudden arrow emphasize?

answers: They move from witnessing events to fearing and declaring God’s work
They become partners in the wicked plan
challenge.explanation: The final verse says that all men fear and declare the work of God.
challenge.q: How does the response of the people change in these verses?

paragraphs.title: The Righteous Rejoice and Trust in God

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The righteous shall be glad in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom shall the righteous be glad?

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “and shall trust in him,” referring to the LORD.
easy.q: In whom shall the righteous trust?

easy.explanation: The verse ends with “all the upright in heart shall glory.”
easy.q: Who shall glory in the LORD?

answers: Their joy comes from relying on God
Their joy comes from joining the wicked
Their joy comes from needing no protection
medium.explanation: The verse joins gladness with trust in the LORD.
medium.q: What is the connection between the righteous being glad and trusting in God?

answers: People who are sincere and morally straight
medium.explanation: The expression describes those whose hearts are upright and sincere.

answers: It changes from danger and fear to joy and trust
It changes from joy to fear
It changes from prayer to complete silence
medium.explanation: After the wicked are judged, the righteous rejoice and trust in the LORD.
medium.q: How does the mood change from the earlier verses to this verse?

answers: The joy and praise extend from one righteous person to all upright people
The righteous person remains completely alone
challenge.explanation: The verse begins with the righteous and ends with all the upright in heart.
challenge.q: What does the movement from “the righteous” to “all the upright in heart” show?

answers: God’s judgment leads the righteous to trust, rejoice, and praise Him
The wicked’s schemes lead to their complete victory
challenge.explanation: The psalm ends with the righteous glad in the LORD and glorying in Him.
challenge.q: How does this verse summarize the main movement of the psalm?

answers: The wicked use secret schemes, while the righteous trust and glory in the LORD
The wicked trust in the LORD, while the righteous lay snares
There is no contrast between them
challenge.explanation: The wicked depend on hidden plots, but the righteous respond with trust and praise.
challenge.q: What is the contrast between the wicked and the righteous?
